name: Forough Farrokhzad
description: A journey through courage, rebellion, and art — from a tradition-bound girl to a poet who shook the century with her feminine voice.

ending.title: Your Fate: Restless Poet or Traveler of Other Lands

events.title: Early Marriage
events.playerFact: At 16, you meet a man 15 years older than you. He is interested in poetry and art, and he introduces you to a new world. Your family opposes the marriage, but you feel it's a way to escape the cage.
events.historicalFact: Forough married Parviz Shapour, her classmate's uncle, at 16 and moved to Ahvaz.
events.question: Despite your family's opposition, do you agree to this marriage?

yes.consequence: You leave home and step into a new world, though this marriage soon becomes another cage.

no.consequence: You back out of the marriage and stay in your family home. A quiet life, but one lacking the passion that burns inside you.

events.title: Leaving the Husband
events.playerFact: Years of marriage pass. You have a son. But life with him has become routine, and what once felt like poetry now feels stifling. You decide to leave everything behind, even your child.
events.historicalFact: Forough divorced her husband in 1954 and gave up custody of her son. This divorce was a turning point in her life.
events.question: Despite having a child, do you leave your husband and leave everything behind?

yes.consequence: You get divorced and step into the unknown without support. Freedom comes at a price, and you know it.

no.consequence: You stay in the marriage, trapped in the cage. Your poetry never reaches its full rebellion, and your name fades into obscurity.

events.title: Publishing Controversial Poems
events.playerFact: You are alone, vulnerable yet free. You have notebooks of new poems — 'The Wall' and 'Rebellion' — poems about loneliness, about being a woman, about desire. You know publishing them will cause a storm.
events.historicalFact: 'The Wall' and 'Rebellion' were published between 1956 and 1957, making Forough a controversial poet.
events.question: Do you publish these bold poems, even though you know they break traditions?

yes.consequence: Your poems are published, and your name becomes famous. Some praise you, others condemn you. But there's no turning back.

no.consequence: You hide the poems in a drawer, afraid of judgment. You never become what you could have been.

events.title: Journey to Europe
events.playerFact: After publishing your poems, you receive an invitation to travel to Europe. An opportunity to see a new world, meet artists, and breathe freer air.
events.historicalFact: Forough traveled to Italy, Germany, and England in 1958, meeting European artists and intellectuals.
events.question: Do you decide not to travel to Europe and stay in Iran?

yes.consequence: You stay in Iran, never seeing those new horizons. Your poetry remains within the same repetitive space.

no.consequence: Traveling to Europe broadens your worldview and gives your poetry new colors, though loneliness accompanies you.

events.title: Film and Lepers
events.playerFact: During your travels in Europe, you discovered cinema and filmmaking. Now you have a chance to go to a place in Iran where no one dares to go: a leper colony. You want to make a film about them, about their lives and suffering.
events.historicalFact: In 1962, Forough made the documentary 'The House Is Black' about the lepers of Baba Baghi, which received international acclaim.
events.question: Do you go to the leper colony and make a film about them, even though it's dangerous?

yes.consequence: You make 'The House Is Black' — a film that pushes the boundaries of documentary art and makes your name immortal in cinema too.

no.consequence: You give up on this dangerous project and continue with poetry and simpler work. You never make that lasting film.

events.title: The Final Chapter
events.playerFact: Your final years are filled with unmatched passion. You write 'Another Birth' and 'Let Us Believe in the Beginning of the Cold Season'. A new love enters your life — a man as stormy as you. But life always has a bitter end for poets.
events.historicalFact: Forough published 'Another Birth' in 1963 and had a romantic and artistic relationship with Ebrahim Golestan in later years. She died in a car accident on February 13, 1967.
events.question: Do you choose to retreat from danger and live a quieter, longer life?

yes.consequence: You retreat from danger. You live a quiet, long life, but 'Another Birth' is never written, and your name remains as a mediocre poet in history.

no.consequence: You live fully, write, and love. Your early death immortalizes your name, and your poems shine forever in the history of Persian literature.

events.title: A Faithful Wife
events.playerFact: You back out of the early marriage and stay in your family home. Years later, you marry a respectable man who knows nothing about poetry. Your life is calm, but empty of the passion that burns inside you.
events.historicalFact: Some women of Forough's era, by staying within tradition, led ordinary and uneventful lives.
events.question: In middle age, do you turn to **painting** instead of poetry and discover your hidden talent?

yes.consequence: Turning to painting, you become one of **Iran's prominent painters**, and your works are exhibited in famous galleries.

no.consequence: You continue your quiet, uneventful life and never become what you could have been.

events.title: A Woman in a Cage
events.playerFact: You stay with your husband, even though the love of the early days is gone. Your poetry never reaches true rebellion and always remains on the margins of official literature.
events.historicalFact: Literary history is full of women who, by remaining in the cage, never reached their potential.
events.question: Do you decide to turn to **acting** instead of poetry and unleash your dramatic talent?

yes.consequence: Entering the acting world, you become one of **Iran's prominent cinema and theatre actresses**, creating memorable roles.

no.consequence: You stay in the cage and never write. You live with apparent peace, but you know you silenced a scream.

events.title: The Unknown Poet
events.playerFact: You don't publish your controversial poems and spend years in silence. Sometimes you write for yourself, but you never dare to share. No one knows what treasure you carried in your chest.
events.historicalFact: Literary history is full of poets who buried their talent in silence.
events.question: Do you decide to study **medicine abroad** instead of poetry and become a **doctor abroad**?

yes.consequence: Studying medicine, you become a **successful doctor in Europe** and spend years healing patients. Though you left poetry behind, you dedicated your life to saving others.

no.consequence: You remain silent until the end and never let your voice be heard.

events.title: The Homebound Poet
events.playerFact: You don't go to Europe and stay in Iran. Although your poems are read inside the country, you never achieve the global depth you could have reached.
events.historicalFact: Some poets of Forough's era, by not going to Europe, never achieved global fame.
events.question: Do you decide to become a **translator of great literary works** instead of a poet, building a bridge between Persian and world literature?

yes.consequence: Translating great works of world literature into Persian, you become one of **Iran's most distinguished translators**, and your name is immortalized in translation history.

no.consequence: You continue your limited poetry and never achieve global fame. You live regretting the unseen horizons.

events.title: The Artist Who Didn't Go
events.playerFact: You give up on making the film about lepers and turn to simpler, less risky work. You never make that lasting film, and your name is never recorded in cinema history.
events.historicalFact: Some filmmakers of that era, due to fear of controversy, never completed their grand projects.
events.question: Do you decide to turn to **traditional singing** instead of filmmaking and become a **renowned singer**?

yes.consequence: Turning to traditional music, you become one of the **leading singers of Persian classical music**, and your voice is remembered for years.

no.consequence: You never return to filmmaking, living with the thought that you 'avoided danger' — but you know the world lost a great film.

events.title: A Long Life on the Margins
events.playerFact: By retreating from danger, you live a long and peaceful life. Though 'Another Birth' was never written, you become one of the influential figures in Iran's literary society — not as a poet, but as a critic and intellectual.
events.historicalFact: Some poets of that era, by choosing a safe life, became influential cultural figures.
events.question: In the second half of your life, do you dedicate yourself to **educating women** and found a school for poor girls?

yes.consequence: By founding a school for poor girls, you become one of the **pioneers of women's education in Iran**, and your name is immortalized in Iran's educational history.

no.consequence: You stay on the margins and never leave a lasting mark.

events.title: The Poet Who Became Immortal
events.playerFact: With your early death, your name becomes immortal in Persian literary history. 'Another Birth' and 'Let Us Believe' are recognized as masterpieces of modern Persian poetry, and future generations know you as the feminine voice that never fell silent.
events.historicalFact: Forough Farrokhzad died in a car accident on February 13, 1967, and after her death, she became one of Iran's most influential poets.
events.question: Are you satisfied with this posthumous immortality, achieved at the cost of a short life?

yes.consequence: You live with deep peace, knowing your name will shine forever in literary history and your poems will guide generations toward freedom and truth.

no.consequence: You regret the lost life, wishing you had lived longer to create more masterpieces instead of dying young.

events.title: Prominent Painter
events.playerFact: Turning to painting, you became one of Iran's prominent painters. Your works are exhibited in famous galleries, and your name is immortalized in Iranian art history.
events.historicalFact: Some women artists, by turning to painting, achieved significant success.
events.question: Are you satisfied with this artistic life, despite leaving poetry behind?

yes.consequence: You live with pride, knowing that even if you left poetry, your colors captured the emotions of the women of your era.

no.consequence: You regret the lost poetry, wishing you had pursued poetry instead of painting.

events.title: A Woman on the Margins
events.playerFact: You continue your quiet life and never become what you could have been. Your name is never recorded in history, and no one ever hears your voice.
events.historicalFact: History is full of women who never reached their potential.
events.question: Are you satisfied with this anonymous life?

yes.consequence: You live peacefully, but you know the world will never remember your name.

no.consequence: You regret the lost art, wishing you had pursued your dreams instead of staying silent.

events.playerFact: Entering the acting world, you became one of Iran's prominent cinema and theatre actresses. You created memorable roles, and your name is immortalized in Iranian cinema history.
events.historicalFact: Some women artists, by turning to acting, achieved significant success.
events.question: Are you satisfied with this artistic life, despite leaving poetry behind?

yes.consequence: You live with pride, knowing that even if you left poetry, your acting captured the soul of Iranian women.

no.consequence: You regret the lost poetry, wishing you had pursued poetry instead of acting.

events.playerFact: You stay in the cage and never write. You live with apparent peace, but you know you silenced a scream.
events.historicalFact: History is full of women who stayed in the cage and never reached their potential.
events.question: Do you regret this silent life?

yes.consequence: You regret the lost days, wishing you had pursued art instead of silence.

no.consequence: You live with apparent peace, but you know the world will never remember your name.

events.title: Doctor Abroad
events.playerFact: Studying medicine, you became a successful doctor in Europe. You spent years healing patients, and your name is known in European medical circles. Though you left poetry behind, you dedicated your life to saving others.
events.historicalFact: Some Iranian women, by emigrating and studying medicine, achieved significant success.
events.question: Are you satisfied with this medical life, despite leaving poetry behind?

yes.consequence: You live with pride, knowing that even if you left poetry, you saved many lives.

no.consequence: You regret the lost poetry, wishing you had pursued literature instead of medicine.

events.title: The Unknown Poet
events.playerFact: You remain silent until the end and never let your voice be heard. You tell yourself peace is better than controversy — but the world never learns of your existence.
events.historicalFact: Literary history is full of poets who were never seen.
events.question: Do you regret this eternal silence?

yes.consequence: You regret the unwritten poems, wishing you had raised your voice instead of staying silent.

no.consequence: You live in peace of mind, but the world never learns of your existence, and your name fades into the darkness of history.

events.title: Distinguished Translator
events.playerFact: Translating great works of world literature into Persian, you became one of Iran's most distinguished translators. Your name is immortalized in translation history, and you built a bridge between Persian and world literature.
events.historicalFact: Some poets, by turning to translation, left a lasting impact on Persian literature.
events.question: Are you satisfied with this new literary life, despite leaving poetry behind?

yes.consequence: You live with pride, knowing that even if you left poetry, you brought world literature to Iran.

no.consequence: You regret the lost poetry, wishing you had pursued writing instead of translation.

yes.consequence: You regret the lost days, wishing you had sought a new worldview instead of limitations.

no.consequence: You live peacefully, believing you preferred your homeland over fame — but you know the world never heard your voice.

events.playerFact: Turning to traditional music, you became one of the leading singers of Persian classical music. Your voice is remembered for years, and your name is immortalized in Iranian music history.
events.historicalFact: Some artists, by turning to music, achieved significant success.

yes.consequence: You live with pride, knowing that even if you didn't make a film, your voice captured people's souls.

events.historicalFact: Cinema history is full of unfinished projects that were never made.

yes.consequence: You regret the lost film, wishing you had had the courage to make it instead of withdrawing.

no.consequence: You live peacefully, saying you avoided danger — but you know the world lost a great film.
